contract_plain_english: In its discussion of wave propagation in heterogeneous media, the source says finite-volume methods are a natural choice because each grid cell can be assigned its own material properties through appropriate averaging of material parameters over the volume enclosed by that cell (raw PDF page 30, printed page 8, Section 1.4, first paragraph). Heterogeneity may vary slowly or include sharp interfaces with jumps in material parameters (raw PDF page 29, printed page 7, Section 1.4, final paragraph). This is a qualitative modeling claim. The material-averaging formula and its admissibility conditions are not specified by 'appropriate averaging' (raw PDF page 30, printed page 8). The earlier integral-divided-by-volume definition explicitly concerns the cell average of the solution q and does not by itself settle the material-averaging choice (raw PDF page 27, printed page 5, Section 1.2).
